editorial.description_en: Ripe fruit on a bare branch. The highest-chroma entry in the corpus, and the only one that is unambiguously a red.
editorial.description_ja: 熟した実のような、こい赤。
editorial.contemporaryNote_en: The corpus ceiling for chroma. It is here so that the Atlas has one colour that a screen renders convincingly and a camera estimate does not, which is a difference worth being able to show.

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.530, C 0.134, h 28.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 実 (mi, fruit) + 赤 (aka, red). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Fruit Red" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 実赤. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — yaki-tsuchi at ΔE00 8.3, sabi-iwa at ΔE00 10.1, yama-moe at ΔE00 10.6. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (208°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
